clue.text: Realistic show must be awful crap to amuse (they say) the awful cast

indicators.note: something awful is in a dreadful state, so the word after it is jumbled into a new order

taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A critic sneers that a supposedly realistic production is rubbish, with a dreadful cast.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is in two lights, 1 and 6 across. Both pieces read as words: a realistic show is a practical one, and Cats is the show; T.S. Eliot's Old Possum's Book of Practical Cats inspired the musical.
explanation.definitionFit: Realistic means practical, and Cats is the famous stage musical, so a sensible musical is wittily read as these words.

clue.text: With loads of room for the "i" in "semivowel"

indicators.note: putting the letter in the word means it is placed inside that word

parts.note: a palatal is a sound made with the tongue against the hard palate, such as the semivowel y
the letter itself

explanation.surface: A phonetics note about where the letter i sits in the word semivowel.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks suggest we look at the letters of 'semivowel' itself, but it must be replaced by a kind of semivowel before the i goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: A palatial building is grand like a palace, so it has space in abundance.

clue.text: Essential for lamb learning to walk

indicators.note: what is essential to something lies at its core, so the letters sit inside the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A newborn lamb needs something before it can take its first steps.
explanation.definitionFit: To amble is to stroll at an easy, leisurely pace on foot.

clue.text: Slides that can't be hidden?

parts.note: surface reading: photographic slides or sheets for an overhead projector
setter's reading: things so clear that you can see right through them, so nothing about them is concealed

explanation.walkthrough: Projector slides are called by a name that also describes anything see-through, which is why they cannot hide anything.
explanation.definitionFit: Overhead projector sheets and photographic slides are named for being see-through, and anything see-through conceals nothing.

clue.text: Many outside Tyneside should be hit on the head

indicators.note: one thing outside another wraps round it, holding it within

parts.note: a crowd is many people
Tyneside, around Newcastle, is in England's North East, abbreviated NE

explanation.surface: A mob in the North East is getting violent and someone is going to be clobbered.
explanation.definitionFit: To crown someone is informal slang for striking them on the top of the skull.

clue.text: Having had some lager — dead drunk at the start — his problem?

the words just before are wanted only for their opening letters

parts.note: the first letter of each word
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A young man has had a few beers and was legless early on; is drink his problem?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition as well as the wordplay: the lad who drinks lager until he is drunk is behaving in this way.
explanation.definitionFit: Laddish behaviour is the loud, boozy conduct of young men out drinking beer together.

clue.text: See 1

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.walkthrough: The speaker of the clue, who would not drink retsina, is the answer, so the definition works in the first person.

explanation.definitionFit: Simony is the ecclesiastical offence of buying or selling church posts or pardons.

explanation.definitionFit: To act contemptuously is to behave with open disdain and derision toward others.

clue.text: Sign of opposition to Tory big guns?

parts.note: the Liberals were the traditional rival party of the Conservatives in Britain
the Royal Artillery, the army's gunners

explanation.surface: Is there an emblem showing resistance to the Conservative heavyweights?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big guns' looks like party grandees but means the Royal Artillery.
explanation.definitionFit: Libra, the scales, is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: Senior citizens' concession returned, all with book of 1 6

parts.note: the old are the senior citizens

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a sop is a small concession made to pacify someone
the sum is the whole, all of it

explanation.surface: A pensioners' discount has been brought back, along with a volume of verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 1 6 is the answer to 1 and 6 across, and the book is T.S. Eliot's Old Possum's Book of Practical Cats; Old Possum was Ezra Pound's nickname for Eliot.
explanation.definitionFit: The cat poems are titled as belonging to this persona, so the owner of that book is him.

clue.text: Crime needs time and cause

parts.note: T is the standard abbreviation for time
a cause is a reason

explanation.surface: Committing an offence requires opportunity and motive.
explanation.definitionFit: Treason, betraying one's country or sovereign, is the gravest criminal offence against the state.

clue.text: Progressing along lines?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: under way and advancing, as a plan is
second meaning, read literally: aboard a carriage running on railway lines

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for under way is also, read literally, where a rail passenger is.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means arranged and under way, and a rail passenger travelling the tracks is literally aboard a carriage.

clue.text: Opening of epic play — what can hold a note in song, if historic

parts.note: Ma is mother; the 's means 'has'

parts.note: Sark is one of the Channel Islands

explanation.surface: Mum's gold coin holds something from the Channel Islands, revealing her as a resistance fighter.
explanation.walkthrough: The island loses its last letter before going inside the coin, between its I and D. A sovereign is an old British gold pound coin.
explanation.definitionFit: A maquisard was a member of the French wartime Resistance, a guerrilla partisan fighter.

clue.text: Absentee of 1 6 makes a hole under mountain

a cavity is a hole

explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'under' places the hole below the mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: In Eliot's cat poems the Mystery Cat is famous for never being there when a crime is discovered.

clue.text: Antique cover — one managed to survive into last century

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the monarch whose head appears on the stamps of an old philatelic envelope, called a cover

definitions.text: one managed to survive into last century
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the monarch who died in January 1901, just inside the twentieth century

explanation.walkthrough: To stamp collectors a cover is a posted envelope; an old one bears the Penny Black with this monarch's head.
explanation.definitionFit: The long-reigning Victorian monarch appears on early postage stamps and died in 1901, after the twentieth century began.

clue.text: No fishing possible with such a financial result?

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read literally: when a fisherman's mesh has gone missing he cannot fish
second meaning: the bottom line in accounts when costs exceed income

explanation.walkthrough: The accounting term is read literally as the disappearance of a fishing mesh.
explanation.definitionFit: In accounts, the overall deficit after expenses exceed income is the figure described here, and a missing mesh stops any angling.

clue.text: House the French talk about

explanation.definitionFit: A lazybones is one who does little, and the comparative of idle means more inactive or more futile.

clue.text: In and out of season?
